prerequisites: Completion of first-year courses, especially Mathematics I and II and Physics I and II.

learning_outcomes.text: Students should have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.

Students should know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Students should be able to transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Ability to apply new technologies, including information and communication technologies.
Knowledge of applied thermodynamics and heat transfer. Basic principles and their application to solving engineering problems.
Knowledge of the basic principles of fluid mechanics and their application to solving problems in the field of engineering. Calculation of pipes, channels, and fluid systems.

syllabus_topics: First and second principle of thermodynamics.
Analysis of substances. Physical and chemical behavior.
Heat transfer by conduction, convection, and radiation.
Closed systems: first and second principle.
Open systems: first and second principle.
Vapor power cycles and refrigeration cycles.
Practical Session 1: Analysis of processes in closed systems.
Practical Session 2: Thermodynamic properties of pure substances.
Practical Session 3: Study and analysis of thermodynamic cycles with Termograf.
Practical Session 4: Study of convection in different geometries.
Practical Session 5: Experimental confirmation of the black-body radiation law.
teaching_methods: Lectures in large groups (master classes, presentations, blackboard demonstrations).
Classes in small groups (computer labs, exercise resolution, practical activities, seminars).

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities

assessment_rules: The final grade consists of a semester-end exam (90%), laboratory practices (5%), and attendance/participation (5%). To pass the exam, a minimum of 50% is required in each of its 3-5 problems, and an overall score of 5 points. The scores for practices and attendance are only added if the exam grade is 5 or higher. Mandatory attendance at laboratory practices and submission of reports are required to pass the course.
